content: 1. When linagliptin is administered with a CYP3A4 inducer, adjustments in therapy are recommended to ensure therapeutic efficacy. 2. Linezolid increases phenobarbital levels by reducing its metabolism, but the clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. 3. Phenobarbital decreases liothyronine levels by enhancing its metabolism, though the clinical impact remains uncertain. 4. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while lisdexamfetamine reduces it. The interaction's effect is unclear, so caution and close monitoring are advised. 5. Belladonna alkaloids and lofepramine both reduce cholinergic effects, while phenobarbital and lofepramine increase sedation. Barbiturates may exacerbate adverse effects, including respiratory depression, when combined with toxic doses of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs). With therapeutic doses of TCAs, barbiturates increase metabolism and reduce blood concentrations of TCAs. Close monitoring is necessary. 6. Phenobarbital decreases lomitapide levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. 7. Phenobarbital reduces lonafarnib levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers is contraindicated. 8. Lonapegsomatropin decreases phenobarbital levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Limited data suggest growth hormone treatment increases CYP450-mediated clearance. Caution is advised with sensitive CYP substrates. 9. Phenobarbital reduces loperamide levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Close monitoring is required. 10. Phenobarbital decreases lopinavir levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 11. Phenobarbital and loprazolam both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Phenobarbital reduces loratadine levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Both drugs increase sedation. Close monitoring is advised. 13. Phenobarbital and lorazepam both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Phenobarbital reduces lorlatinib levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A inducers is contraindicated. Discontinue the inducer for three plasma half-lives before initiating lorlatinib. 15. Phenobarbital and lormetazepam both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Phenobarbital reduces losartan levels or effects via CYP3A4 and CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear, but close monitoring is recommended. 17. Phenobarbital decreases lovastatin levels or effects via P-glycoprotein efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. 18. Phenobarbital and loxapine both increase sedation. Loxapine enhances the effects of belladonna alkaloids through pharmacodynamic synergy. Belladonna alkaloids reduce loxapine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. These interactions apply only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Phenobarbital reduces lumacaftor/ivacaftor levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers is contraindicated, as it may reduce the effectiveness of lumacaftor/ivacaftor. 20. Phenobarbital and lumateperone both increase sedation. Phenobarbital reduces lumateperone levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. 21. Phenobarbital reduces lumefantrine levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers is contraindicated, as it may lead to decreased serum concentrations and loss of antimalarial efficacy. 22. Phenobarbital reduces lurasidone levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Phenobarbital reduces lurbinectedin levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. 24. Phenobarbital reduces macimorelin levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration may lead to false-positive test results. Discontinue strong CYP3A4 inducers with sufficient washout time before testing. 25. Phenobarbital reduces macitentan levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers should be avoided. 26. Belladonna alkaloids and maprotiline both reduce cholinergic effects, while phenobarbital and maprotiline increase sedation. Barbiturates may exacerbate adverse effects, including respiratory depression, when combined with toxic doses of TCAs. Close monitoring is necessary. 27. Phenobarbital reduces maraviroc levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Phenobarbital and marijuana both increase sedation. Phenobarbital reduces marijuana levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Phenobarbital reduces mavacamten levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 30. Phenobarbital reduces mavorixafor levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. 31. Phenobarbital and meclizine both increase sedation. Belladonna alkaloids and meclizine both reduce cholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Phenobarbital reduces medroxyprogesterone levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Contraceptive failure is possible. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 33. Phenobarbital and mefloquine may reduce each other's effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Phenobarbital reduces melatonin levels or effects via CYP1A2 metabolism. Both drugs increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Phenobarbital reduces meloxicam levels or effects via CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear, but close monitoring is recommended. 36. Phenobarbital and meperidine both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Phenobarbital and meprobamate both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Phenobarbital reduces mestranol levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Contraceptive failure is possible. Alternative drugs should be considered. 39. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while metaproterenol reduces it. The interaction's effect is unclear, so caution and close monitoring are advised. 40. Phenobarbital and metaxalone both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Phenobarbital reduces methadone levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while methamphetamine reduces it. The interaction's effect is unclear, so caution and close monitoring are advised. 43. Methazolamide and phenobarbital may interact through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of anticonvulsant-induced osteomalacia. Close monitoring is recommended. 44. Phenobarbital and methocarbamol both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Methohexital and phenobarbital both increase sedation. Alternative drugs should be considered. 46. Phenobarbital increases methoxyflurane toxicity by enhancing its metabolism to nephrotoxic compounds. Co-administration is contraindicated. 47. Belladonna alkaloids and methscopolamine both reduce cholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Methsuximide and phenobarbital both increase sedation. Methsuximide reduces phenobarbital effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance is unclear, but close monitoring is recommended. 49. Methylene blue and belladonna alkaloids both increase serotonin levels. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs considered. 50. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while methylenedioxymethamphetamine reduces it. The interaction's effect is unclear, so caution and close monitoring are advised. 51. Methylphenidate increases phenobarbital levels or effects through an unknown mechanism. Monitor for increased serum concentrations or toxicity of phenobarbital when methylphenidate is initiated or its dose is increased. 52. Methylphenidate transdermal reduces phenobarbital metabolism, increasing its levels or effects. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 53. Phenobarbital reduces methylprednisolone levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Phenobarbital and metoclopramide intranasal may increase each other's effects. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs considered. 55. Phenobarbital reduces metoprolol levels by increasing its metabolism. Consider a higher beta-blocker dose during co-administration. Atenolol, sotalol, and nadolol are less likely to be affected. 56. Phenobarbital reduces metyrapone effects through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unclear, but close monitoring is recommended. 57. Phenobarbital reduces mexiletine levels or effects via CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Phenobarbital reduces miconazole vaginal levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unclear, but close monitoring is recommended. 59. Phenobarbital reduces midazolam levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Midazolam intranasal and phenobarbital may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 61. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while midodrine reduces it. The interaction's effect is unclear, so caution and close monitoring are advised. 62. Phenobarbital reduces midostaurin levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers should be avoided. 63. Phenobarbital reduces mifepristone levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended by the manufacturer. 64. Mipomersen and phenobarbital may increase each other's toxicity. Both drugs have the potential to elevate hepatic enzymes, so liver function tests should be monitored. 65. Phenobarbital reduces mirtazapine levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended.
